risk: IOPS backtests never reach the recent data. All 20 IOPS series stop predicting around December 2022 while their actuals run to 2023-07-20.
evidence: 22 of 90 series have newest_observation_preserved=FALSE: all 20 IOPS and 2 CPU (CHN-Gallatin). IOPS carries 8-23 missing calendar days per series, so late origins fail the contiguous-window test and only 5-6 of 11 sampled origins survive.
impact: Roughly seven months of the most recent IOPS history would never be backtested. That directly contradicts the owner rule that the newest observations must be preserved for validation.
mitigation: Adopt Decision D2 below: relax the test window from 'exactly 30 contiguous days' to 'at least N observations inside the 30-day window', and always force an origin at max_date - 30 so the newest data is always the last thing predicted.
resolution: Owner approved D2 Option B on 2026-08-23. Recomputed contract: 90 of 90 series now reach their max actual date, up from 68. All 20 IOPS series recovered: last target moved from around 2022-12-26 to 2023-07-20. No dates were filled or invented.

risk: The reference generator RAISES on a non-contiguous test window instead of skipping it.
evidence: run_v6_17_viewer_backtests.py, training_and_test(): `if len(training) < LAGS+HORIZON+5 or len(test) != HORIZON_DAYS: raise ValueError`. HDD has 0 calendar gaps so this never fired. SSD has 2, CPU 1-7, IOPS 8-23.
impact: Reusing the reference code unmodified would crash on the very first gappy origin rather than degrade gracefully.
mitigation: P5 must wrap origin evaluation in the failure policy and pre-filter origins using the window contract produced here, instead of discovering invalid origins at fit time.
resolution: P5 must pre-filter origins using v6_24_p5a_backtest_window_contract_D2_APPROVED.csv rather than letting training_and_test() raise. No owner decision needed.

risk: The governed catalog spells the champion ETS_Explicit; the code and the HDD artifact both use 'ETS Explicit' with a space.
evidence: Registry key is 'ETS Explicit'; the HDD parquet model_name column also uses the space.
impact: A naive lookup by the governed name would raise KeyError, and a naive union with the HDD artifact would create two distinct model identities for one model.
mitigation: Map explicitly in P5 and write the space form so P5 output unions cleanly with HDD. Recorded in the model catalog contract; never substitute silently.

risk: The 3 neural models dominate runtime and are the least stable.
evidence: FNAR-V2, NLIN-DLIN_FIXED and SMLP-TCN are MLP-based. The HDD reference isolated them in a separate phase with its own budget.
impact: A neural failure late in the run could consume the budget and leave the cheap models incomplete.
mitigation: Two-phase execution: run the 12 non-neural models first and checkpoint, then the 3 neural models. Mirrors the HDD reference structure.

risk: Valid origins per series vary from 5 to 10 across the cohort.
evidence: SSD 10 of 11, CPU 8-10 of 11, IOPS 5-6 of 11.
impact: Accuracy is averaged over different numbers of origins per metric, so cross-metric comparisons are not like-for-like.
mitigation: Record valid_origin_count per series in the output and surface it wherever accuracy is reported in P6/P7.

risk: Prediction row volume is modest and not a risk.
evidence: 24,000 target dates x 15 models = 360,000 rows, roughly 90.0 MB uncompressed. The HDD artifact alone is 2.4M rows at 13.6 MB compressed.
Import check: 8 of 8 OK; none missing.
impact: An abort at startup rather than mid-run.
mitigation: Startup capability check before any fitting, per the failure policy.

risk: A one-day offset between predicted_value and actual_value would be invisible but would corrupt every accuracy number downstream.
evidence: The HDD artifact stores target date in `date` while also carrying forecast_start_date and horizon_days, so an off-by-one is easy to introduce when renaming columns.
impact: Every accuracy metric and ranking in P6 would be wrong while looking plausible.
mitigation: Mandatory post-batch assertion: join predictions back to actuals_normalized on (series_id, target_date) and require an exact actual_value match, plus prediction_date == target_date and train_end_date < target_date on every row.
